newsitem.title: USA: Mark gains as French poll concerns spark EMU doubt.
newsitem.headline: Mark gains as French poll concerns spark EMU doubt.

text.p: Growing uncertainty ahead of French general elections sent the mark soaring on Wednesday as traders pondered if the results of the poll might help derail plans for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), U.S. analysts said.
The mark gained against a broad array of European currencies, climbing to a 16-week high against the French franc and an eight-week peak versus the Spanish peseta.
Reports that the central banks of Spain and Sweden intervened to support their currencies against the mark also swept through the market.

"Yesterday, the perception was ... a socialist victory wouldn't damage the prospects of the euro, but I think suddenly the market's realizing maybe that's not true," said Ron Leven, a currency strategist at J.P. Morgan and Co Inc.

"If there is euro abandonment being priced into the market, that's going to affect the lira and peseta more than it really ultimately will the French franc ... even if it is triggered by a French event," he added.
Leven cited concern French socialists may not win a strong enough position to have a majority on their own and might have to rely on the Communists, who he said have been against currency union.

The final round of French general elections is set for Sunday. The French Socialist party favors a less stringent interpretation of the criteria that countries must meet in order to qualify for EMU, which is scheduled to debut in January 1999.
Brian McCarthy, market analyst at Ruesch International, noted that apparent flows of funds coming out of France seemed to pull the mark higher.
In addition, McCarthy also cited doubts about plans for the single European currency, but he talked of a possible delay.

"Another potential issue is that the Germans will hint that they are inclined to delay the launch of EMU rather than water down the Maastricht Treaty," McCarthy said. "And that, of course, would be hugely mark positive."
